examples.appendix_structure: ONE Multimedia Appendix, captioned on the article page as "Multimedia Appendix 1 — Supplementary materials that support the main analyses. DOCX File, 1394 KB". I downloaded the DOCX and extracted its paragraph text. It opens with a title page reading "Supplementary Materials 3" followed by a dotted-leader table of contents, then a sequence of NUMBERED SECTION HEADINGS, each introducing its own tables/figures. The headings, verbatim and in order: "Supplementary 1. Participant Flow description." / "Supplementary 2. Statistical recording issue description" / "Supplementary 3. Regression Models comparing tracks started versus completed during statistical recording error" (contains "Table S1.", "Table S2.") / "Supplementary 4. Country of Residence Descriptives for Full Sample." ("Table S3.") / "Supplementary 5. Assessment of Relationship between Sociodemographic Factors and Engagement" ("Table S4.") / "Supplementary 6. Correlations between predictor variables and engagement" ("Table S5.") / "Supplementary 7. Semi-partial correlations between predictor variables and engagement." ("Table S6.") / "Supplementary 8. Main regression model assessing relationship between predictors and engagement" ("Table S7.") / "Supplementary 9. Regression Model with Expectation and Mental Health components." ("Table S8.", "Table S9.") / "Supplementary 10. Tests for Normality, Linearity and Multicollinearity" ("Figure S1.", "Figure S2.") / "Supplementary 11. Principal Component Analysis (PCA)" ("Table S10." through "Table S13.") / "Supplementary 12. Scatterplots comparing factor score with engagement level..." ("Figure S3." through "Figure S7."). So: a single appendix with 12 internal sections, tables numbered S1-S13 continuously across sections, figures numbered S1-S7 separately. Sections are labelled "Supplementary N.", NOT "Part A/B/C".
examples.how_cited_in_text: The published main text cites BOTH internal sections and individual tables, always in JMIR's "<item> in Multimedia Appendix N" grammar. Verbatim from the article HTML: "See Figure 1 and Supplementary 1 in Multimedia Appendix 1 for a detailed description of participant flow."; "...the glitch was unlikely to have seriously affected the data (Supplementary 2 and Supplementary 3 in Multimedia Appendix 1)."; "...(Figures 3 and 6 and Supplementary 4 and Supplementary 5 in Multimedia Appendix 1)."; "Multicollinearity was observed within the regression (Figure S2 in Multimedia Appendix 1)."; "...the amount of variance was reduced substantially (R2=0.02; Table S7 in Multimedia Appendix 1)." Note the word order: never "Multimedia Appendix 1, Table S7".

examples.citation: Improving the Prognostic Evaluation Precision of Hospital Outcomes for Heart Failure Using Admission Notes and Clinical Tabular Data: Multimodal Deep Learning Model. Journal of Medical Internet Research. 2024;26:e54363. DOI 10.2196/54363. https://www.jmir.org/2024/1/e54363 (appendix file: https://jmir.org/api/download?alt_name=jmir_v26i1e54363_app1.docx)
examples.appendix_structure: ONE Multimedia Appendix, captioned "Multimedia Appendix 1 — Additional statistics. DOCX File , 466 KB". I downloaded the DOCX and extracted its text. Internal structure is completely FLAT: a single word "Appendix" as the opening line, then no section headings at all, just a run of captioned items. Verbatim, in file order: "Figure S1.  An example of clinical notes at admission", "Figure S2. Network architecture of feature fusion.", "Figure S3. Comparison with the approach of concatenating all features directly.", "Figure S4. Comparison with different epoch numbers", "Figure S5. Comparison with different reduction dimension of text feature", "Figure S6. Interpretable predictions of an example", then "Table S1. Names of clinical variables", "Table S2. The missing ratio of all variables in four study cohorts", "Table S2. Detailed performance of the model with different text types of notes" [sic — the third table is mislabelled S2 instead of S3, and the error was published], "Table S4. The characteristic of the development set", "Table S5. The characteristic of the internal validation set", "Table S6. The characteristic of the prospective validation set", "Table S7. The characteristic of the external validation set", "Table S8. Detailed performance of multimodal model vs unimodal models", "Table S9. Performance comparisons of the pretrained Bert model". This is a prediction-model paper with 15 supplementary items in one appendix and zero Parts. It also shows JMIR does not police the appendix internals: all figures are grouped before all tables (not strictly "order of appearance"), and a duplicated S2 number survived to publication — consistent with the stated policy that MAs are not copyedited.
examples.how_cited_in_text: Main text cites items as "Table S9 (Multimedia Appendix 1)" / "Table Sx in Multimedia Appendix 1" style; e.g. the Results discuss AUROC comparisons referring to "Figure 3 and Table S9 (Multimedia Appendix 1)". No section-level or Part-level locator is used.

examples.citation: Woo S, Yon DK, et al. "Machine Learning Prediction Model for Dyslipidemia and Its Association With Atherothrombotic Events in 3 Independent Cohorts From South Korea, Japan, and the United Kingdom: Algorithm Development and Validation Study." examples.appendix_structure: Closest analog I found to the manuscript in question: multi-country external validation, TRIPOD+AI, variable harmonization, calibration, sensitivity analyses. I downloaded the actual DOCX (medinform_v14i1e81130_app1.docx, 318 KB) and extracted word/document.xml. It is 774 paragraphs and completely FLAT. The only top-level heading in the whole file is the single line "Supplementary Material" (paragraph 0). After the title block, every subsequent heading is an item label, in this exact order: "Table S1. TRIPOD+AI checklist." / "Table S2. Variable harmonization scheme and mapping rules for aligning external cohorts to the discovery cohort." / "Table S3. Baseline characteristics in Japan." / "Table S4. Baseline characteristics in the United Kingdom." / "Table S5. Best hyperparameter combinations for CatBoost and LightGBM." / "Table S6. Variable-wise missingness per cohort." / "Table S7. Sensitivity analyses for model robustness and potential label leakage." / "Table S8. Calibration metrics for the prediction model across cohorts." / "Table S9. Subdistribution hazard ratios (95% CI) ..." then "Figure S1." through "Figure S4.". There is no Part, no Section, no A.1/B.2 numbering, and no grouping headings of any kind. Notably, the harmonization crosswalk -- exactly the content the manuscript puts in "Part A" -- is here simply Table S2 in the flat sequence. The published JMIR caption for the appendix is: "Supplementary tables (S1-S9) and figures (S1-S4) supporting the main findings of this study."
examples.how_cited_in_text: Not captured. I read the appendix caption and the DOCX itself, but medinform.jmir.org served a bot-verification page before I could extract main-text citation sentences, so I am not asserting the in-text wording for this paper.

examples.citation: "Machine Learning Models With Prognostic Implications for Predicting Gastrointestinal Bleeding After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Guiding Personalized Medicine: Multicenter Cohort Study." Journal of Medical Internet Research, 2025;27:e68509. https://www.jmir.org/2025/1/e68509 (DOI 10.2196/68509; PMC11926454). Article type printed on the PDF: Original Paper.
examples.appendix_structure: This is the closest match in SIZE to the manuscript in question: Multimedia Appendix 1 is a 6.6 MB Word file (jmir_v27i1e68509_app1.doc) containing Tables S1-S19 and Figures S1-S6 -- more supplementary tables than the 22 described. I downloaded the file and extracted its UTF-16 text streams. It is FLAT, with an auto-generated table of contents (the extracted strings contain Word PAGEREF/_Toc field codes with page numbers, e.g. "Table S1. The Calculation Process, Formula, and Results of Sample Size Determination.\tPAGEREF _Toc12023 \h 8"). The item sequence is Figures S1-S6 and Tables S1-S19, including "Table S2. Admission Features for Machine Learning Models", "Table S3. ICD-9/ICD-10 Codes are Used to Identify Chronic Comorbidities and Procedures", "Table S5. Model Hyperparameter Settings, Ranges, and Rationale", "Table S9. Results of Five Feature Selection Methods", "Table S10. Optimal Hyperparameters for Each Model Configuration", up to "Table S19.". No "Part A/B/C" headings appear anywhere in the extracted text; the only structural device is the TOC with page numbers. This is the key practical lesson: a ~30-page, 25-item JMIR appendix solves navigation with a hyperlinked table of contents, not with Parts.
examples.how_cited_in_text: Main text cites items individually by S-number, always with the table first and the appendix second: "Baseline characteristics stratified by GIBCG occurrence are compared in Tables S6-S8 in Multimedia Appendix 1."; "The calculations process, formulas, and results are presented in Table S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1."; "Table S2 in Multimedia Appendix 1 provides the definitions of each feature." No citation of a Part or section.

examples.citation: "Machine Learning for the Prediction of Procedural Case Durations Developed Using a Large Multicenter Database: Algorithm Development and Validation Study." JMIR AI, 2023;2:e44909. https://ai.jmir.org/2023/1/e44909 (DOI 10.2196/44909; PMC11041482). Article type: Algorithm Development and Validation Study.
examples.appendix_structure: Multimedia Appendix 1 is a 2.8 MB DOCX (ai_v2i1e44909_app1.docx), 1009 paragraphs, containing tables, figures AND long methods/code prose -- i.e. the mixed-content case the author is worried about. I downloaded and extracted it. It opens with the single word "SUPPLEMENT", then the manuscript title, then a table of contents. The organizing headings are BY CONTENT TYPE, not by Part: "Supplementary Tables", "Supplementary Figures", "Supplementary Code". Tables run flat S1-S6 ("Table S1. List of health care centers included in data set" ... "Table S6. Columns (features) dropped by machine learning algorithm at each time point"), figures flat S1-S2. Only the code block gets a letter-prefixed numbering, and it is a C-series, not a Part series: "C1. R Code for Data Processing", "C2. R Code: Training and Testing ML Models", "C3. R Code: Making Predictions Using Created Machine Learning Models". This is the nearest thing to Part-style division that I found in JMIR, and it is still content-type grouping (Tables / Figures / Code) with S- and C- item numbers, never "Part A".
examples.how_cited_in_text: "A list of included centers is provided in Table S1 of Multimedia Appendix 1."; "The number of cases at each deidentified center is provided in Table S2 in Multimedia Appendix 1."; "Study population baseline characteristics, summarizing all features included in the models, are available in Table S3 in Multimedia Appendix 1."; "Permutation feature importance for each time point model is shown in Figure S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1." The prose/code block is cited without any Part label: "The code for natural language processing is provided along with other data processing code in Multimedia Appendix 1 (refer to R Code for Data Processing)." -- i.e. by quoting the heading name, not a Part letter.

examples.appendix_structure: THE ONE CLEAR "PART" CASE I FOUND. Single supplementary PDF explicitly split into two lettered parts by cohort. Verbatim from the article full text: "Results of all 168 patients are given in Supplementary Appendix Part A Tables 1-4"; "Supplementary Appendix Part B Table S4 provides important..."; "...are given in Supplementary Appendix Part B Table S1"; "full data for all evaluated time horizons are given in Supplementary Appendix Part B Table S2"; "Calibration plots are given in the supplementary appendix (Supplementary Appendix Part B Figure S1)".

Description of the 10 lung cancer risk prediction models evaluated in this manuscript and the predictors included in each model."; "Appendix 1 p 2  Supplementary Table 2. examples.citation: Ravaut M, Harish V, Sadeghi H, et al. Development and validation of a machine learning model using administrative health data to predict onset of type 2 diabetes. JAMA Network Open. 2021;4(5):e2111315. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2021.11315. PMC8150694. Supplement file: jamanetwopen-e2111315-s001.pdf, 16 pages.
examples.appendix_structure: The JAMA convention in its purest form - flat, interleaved, typed series, no grouping headers whatsoever. Verbatim contents list on p.1 under "Supplementary Online Content": "eFigure 1. Overview of Our Approach / eMethods 1. Instance Creation Process / eTable 1. Comparing Electronic Medical Records vs Administrative Health Data / eTable 2. Descriptions of Administrative Health Datasets Used / eMethods 2. Feature Engineering / eMethods 3. Model Development and Evaluation / eFigure 2. Ablation Study / eFigure 3. Feature Contribution / eFigure 4. Model Precision and Recall Curves / eTable 3. Results With Other Buffer Sizes / eTable 4. Comparison Against Logistic Regression Baseline / eReferences". The ordering principle is narrative need, so methods prose (eMethods 1-3) sits BETWEEN tables rather than being pooled into a separate methods block. Closing line: "This supplementary material has been provided by the authors to give readers additional information about their work."
examples.how_cited_in_text: By item, always suffixed "in the Supplement". Verbatim: "Details on the XGBoost model parameters can be found in eMethods 3 in the Supplement"; "...can be found in eTables 1 and 2 in the Supplement"; "Results for different buffer sizes can be found in eTable 3 in the Supplement"; "...are displayed in eFigures 2, 3, and 4 and eTable 3 in the Supplement"; "XGBoost was compared with logistic regression in eTable 4 in the Supplement".

examples.citation: Ganguli I, Simpkin AL, Lupo C, et al. Cascades of care after incidental findings in a US national survey of physicians. JAMA Network Open. 2019;2(10):e1913325. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2019.13325. Supplement file: jamanetwopen-2-e1913325-s001.pdf, 17 pages.
examples.appendix_structure: Shows how the JAMA family handles MORE THAN ONE prose block: it NUMBERS the appendices rather than lettering Parts. Verbatim contents list: "eAppendix 1. examples.appendix_structure: The Nature-portfolio convention: a front contents list of four independently numbered typed series, no Parts, no sections. On JMIR's own rules, "Parts" are neither required nor forbidden — but two things about the current draft do conflict with what JMIR writes down, and neither has anything to do with the Part structure per se.

1. THE IN-TEXT CITATIONS ARE THE REAL PROBLEM, NOT THE PARTS. JMIR prescribes exactly one grammar, with the appendix number LAST: "...as shown in Figure S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1" and "...(Table S2 in Multimedia Appendix 3)". The draft's "Multimedia Appendix 1, Table S7" inverts that and will be rewritten in copyediting. Fix it to "Table S7 in Multimedia Appendix 1" regardless of what happens to the Parts. Likewise "Multimedia Appendix 1, Part D" has no JMIR-defined form — "Part D" is not a locator JMIR recognizes anywhere in its knowledge base.

2. THE ONLY BINDING RULE ABOUT THE APPENDIX INTERIOR IS THE NUMBERING: "Each appendix must number items as S1, S2, S3... (separate numbering for figures and tables in one file) in order of appearance." The draft describes 22 tables but only S1-S16, and puts Part D (Supplementary Methods) last while Part A (which contains no tables) comes first. As long as the S-numbers run 1, 2, 3... top to bottom through the file, the Part structure does not break this rule. But 22 tables must carry 22 numbers (S1-S22), or the extras must be figures numbered S1, S2... in their own sequence. Worth auditing.

3. NOTHING IN JMIR PROHIBITS PARTS, AND SECTIONED APPENDICES DO GET PUBLISHED. JMIR states twice that "MAs are not copyedited by the publishing team" and that appendices are "published largely as submitted" — the interior is the author's. I verified a 2026 JMIR mHealth paper (10.2196/79366) whose single Multimedia Appendix 1 is 12 internally numbered sections plus a dotted table of contents, with Tables S1-S13 and Figures S1-S7 running continuously across those sections. So a long, sectioned, single appendix is unquestionably publishable in a JMIR journal.

4. BUT I FOUND NO JMIR PAPER USING "PART A / PART B" LABELS. This is a genuine negative result and I want to be plain about it. I ran targeted site-restricted searches for "Part A"/"Part B" co-occurring with "in Multimedia Appendix 1" across jmir.org and eight sibling journals and got nothing. The one sectioned appendix I actually opened labels its sections "Supplementary 1.", "Supplementary 2.", ... — and its main text cites them the JMIR way: "See Figure 1 and Supplementary 1 in Multimedia Appendix 1..." and "(Supplementary 2 and Supplementary 3 in Multimedia Appendix 1)". That is the published precedent for pointing at a section of an appendix. The other appendix I opened (10.2196/54363, a multimodal prediction-model paper) is entirely flat: no headings at all, just Figure S1-S6 then Table S1-S9. The author is right that Part-labelled appendices are rare-to-absent in JMIR; what is common is either a flat run of S-items or numbered "Supplementary N" sections.

PRACTICAL READING. If the goal is minimum friction with JMIR: keep the sectioning (a 29-page, 22-table appendix needs it), but relabel "Part A/B/C/D" to a form with published precedent — either plain "Supplementary Methods" / "Supplementary Results" headings, or numbered "Supplementary 1., Supplementary 2., ..." as in 10.2196/79366 — and make every table run S1..Sn strictly in order of appearance through the whole file. Then rewrite the two main-text citation strings into JMIR's grammar: "Table S7 in Multimedia Appendix 1", and for the methods pointer either "Supplementary Methods in Multimedia Appendix 1" or, safest, cite the specific numbered section the way the Medito paper does. One further JMIR-specific item that is easy to miss: the appendix must carry its own complete stand-alone reference list, and it must not begin with a title page or the words "Multimedia Appendix 1" — JMIR adds that label automatically at typesetting and a self-applied label produces a duplicate ("Multimedia appendix 1. Supplementary file 1...").

WHERE THE RULES ACTUALLY LIVE. The JMIR Instructions for Authors page itself (https://www.jmir.org/author-information/instructions-for-authors) says almost nothing about appendices. I searched its full rendered text; the only substantive mention is a line item in the IMRD format list, placed between "Abbreviations" and "References": "[optional] Multimedia Appendix of supplementary files (e.g. a PowerPoint presentation of a conference talk about the study, additional screenshots of a website, mpeg/ Quicktime video or audio files, or Excel, Access, SAS, or SPSS files containing original data)". Plus: "All JMIR Publications journals require adherence to and upload of reporting guidelines and checklists for specific article types... For these article types, a completed checklist must be uploaded in a multimedia appendix." All operative rules are in the knowledge base at support.jmir.org (note: support.jmir.org returns HTTP 403 to plain fetching; I read these pages in a browser).

=== 1. THE CONTROLLING PAGE: "What are the guidelines for supplementary files (figures, multimedia appendices, additional material for reviewers/editors only)?" https://support.jmir.org/hc/en-us/articles/115002199367-What-are-the-guidelines-for-supplementary-files-figures-multimedia-appendices-additional-material-for-reviewers-editors-only (page states "3 months ago Updated") ===

This is the ONLY page that addresses the inside of an appendix. Verbatim:

(a) Multiple items in one appendix — EXPLICITLY ALLOWED, with a mandatory numbering scheme: "Of note, we allow multiple items in a single Multimedia Appendix file. However, please ensure that each individual item (eg, figure or table) is named as "Table S1, Table S2, Figure S1, Figure S2) within the Multimedia Appendix. Each appendix must number items as S1, S2, S3... (separate numbering for figures and tables in one file) in order of appearance." [the unbalanced quotation mark is in the original]

(b) The prescribed in-text citation form — note the word order: "If you wish to specifically cite these supplementary tables or figures in the text to draw the reader's attention to them, please refer to them as follows: / "...as shown in Figure S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1" / "...performed better than the control group (Table S2 in Multimedia Appendix 3)""

(c) One file per appendix: "One file per appendix. Multiple files should not be zipped (compressed, packed) together, they should be uploaded as separate supplementary files and referred to as separate Multimedia Appendices in the manuscript / Exception: if there are multiple separate files all containing computer code, they may be left packed and referred to as one Multimedia Appendix"

(d) Order of mention: "In addition, MAs should be mentioned in sequential order in the main manuscript."

(e) Captions: "Captions of MAs are generated from what is entered in the "caption" field in the database for the file... Please do not include the MA label/number in the caption, like Multimedia Appendix 1 or Supplementary file 2, etc. These labels will be added automatically by our script during typesetting. If you add "Supplementary file 1" to the caption, then this will result in a duplicate label ("Multimedia appendix 1. Supplementary file 1...")."

(f) Not copyedited: "Multimedia Appendices (MAs) are published at the end of a paper. / Note: MAs are not copyedited by the publishing team, and it is therefore the authors' responsibility to ensure relevance, accuracy, and completeness of each MA file."

(g) What belongs there: "Examples of what could be uploaded as an MA include questionnaires, datasets, videos or screencasts, a Powerpoint file, tables too long for the body of the manuscript, PDF files showing multiple screenshots..., files containing the source code of a computer program, or informed consent documents." Also: "Do not include a title (first) page as the manuscript title is likely to change during the production process."

(h) References inside an appendix: "References cited within a multimedia appendix (MA) should have a corresponding, stand-alone reference list within that same MA file, even if some references overlap with the main manuscript's reference list."

(i) File formats: ".png, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt, .pptx, .pdf, .txt, .mov, .mp4, .avi, .zip, .rar, .7z"; Word files "will automatically convert them to PDF files... We recommend converting the Word file to a PDF before uploading so you can ensure the file appears as intended."

=== 2. "How do I add/upload a Multimedia Appendix?" https://support.jmir.org/hc/en-us/articles/115003396688-How-do-I-add-upload-a-Multimedia-Appendix ===
"Do not number in the document itself; eg, the title of your document should be descriptive, although it can simply be "Multimedia Appendix", but it should not be "Multimedia Appendix 1", "Multimedia Appendix 2", etc."
"Do not include the title of the manuscript within the multimedia appendix file as this is likely to change during the copyediting and proofreading processes."
"Note: It is your responsibility to ensure each Multimedia Appendix is referenced in the manuscript (eg, "The instrument can be found in Multimedia Appendix 1"), as appendix files are not copyedited by the journal."
The page also shows the typeset output form: "Multimedia Appendix 1 / Sample screenshots of the interactive website / [PPT file (MS Powerpoint), 3 MB]".

=== 3. "Submitting Your Manuscript to JMIR Publications: A Guide for Authors" https://support.jmir.org/hc/en-us/articles/37982552280987-Submitting-Your-Manuscript-to-JMIR-Publications-A-Guide-for-Authors (updated 10 days before I read it) ===
Section "Multimedia Appendix": "Present valuable, supporting information as multimedia appendices. Each appendix should have a clear and descriptive caption." / "Multimedia appendix files are not edited by the journal. Authors are responsible for ensuring these files are clear and accessible to the reader." / "Each multimedia appendix file must contain its own complete reference list, even if some references also appear in the main manuscript's reference list." / "Reporting checklists are always uploaded as a Multimedia Appendix."
Word count: "Word counts do not include author metadata, references, multimedia appendices, or figure content." / "Move technical details, formulas, or lengthy data to Multimedia Appendices to maintain reader engagement." / "Tables exceeding 1.5 pages in the final PDF (approx. 3 pages in Word) must be moved to a Multimedia Appendix. This is generally non-negotiable."

=== 4. "How many tables and figures can I include in my article?" https://support.jmir.org/hc/en-us/articles/360021623072-How-many-tables-and-figures-can-I-include-in-my-article ===
"we encourage authors to include no more than 5 tables and no more than 8 figures per article. Please note that additional tables and figures beyond this soft limit can be published alongside the main manuscript as Multimedia Appendices." / "Place all exploratory or incidental findings not related to your stated primary and secondary outcomes in an appendix. For clear and precise scientific writing, remember: sometimes, less is more."

=== 5. "Manuscript Length and Word Count Guidelines" https://support.jmir.org/hc/en-us/articles/115002798327-Manuscript-Length-and-Word-Count-Guidelines ===
"Material commonly placed in multimedia appendices include: extended methodological details / lengthy formulas or derivations / supplementary analyses / expanded datasets / large tables, including those presenting illustrative quotes or detailed literature findings / full versions of tables shown in abbreviated form in the main manuscript"
"Because appendices are published largely as submitted, please ensure they are complete and submission-ready before sending them to us."
"relocating material to an appendix generally does not require further editorial review, provided the scientific content of the manuscript remains unchanged."

=== 6. PAGES THAT DO **NOT** GOVERN APPENDICES (checked, negative) ===
"JMIR House Style and Editorial Guidelines" https://support.jmir.org/hc/en-us/articles/360019504191-JMIR-House-Style-and-Editorial-Guidelines — I read the whole page. Its only appendix-related rule is under 5.2.4: "Multimedia appendix: Define any abbreviations used within the caption." Nothing about internal organization, Parts, or supplementary table numbering.
"How should headings be formatted?" https://support.jmir.org/hc/en-us/articles/360017464552-How-should-headings-be-formatted — the H1-H6 rules, title case, "there should be a minimum of 2 subheadings per primary section if a subheading is used", and "Avoid citing figures, tables, or references in a heading" apply to the MAIN MANUSCRIPT ("All headings must have a style label called Heading 1 (H1)... this is essential for our XML tagging scripts"). Appendices are not XML-tagged and not copyedited, so these do not bind the appendix.

=== 7. DIRECT ANSWERS TO THE FIVE QUESTIONS ===
- How many appendices are allowed? NO STATED MAXIMUM. I searched the knowledge base and the IFA and found no numeric cap anywhere. The only related constraints are per-file size limits (5 MB PNG, 200 MB video, 255 MB other) and "One file per appendix."
- How named? Authors do not name/number them at all — the file caption is descriptive only, and "Multimedia Appendix N" labels are "added automatically by our script during typesetting", assigned by order of first mention in the main text.
- How cited in text? The prescribed grammar is "<item> in Multimedia Appendix <N>", i.e. "Table S2 in Multimedia Appendix 3" — the appendix number comes LAST. Every MA must be mentioned, and MAs must be "mentioned in sequential order in the main manuscript."
- Is internal structure prescribed? NO. There is no rule permitting or forbidding Parts, sections, or subsection numbering inside an appendix. The single internal rule is the S-numbering of items. JMIR states twice that appendices are not copyedited and are "published largely as submitted", so the internal layout is entirely the author's.
- S1/S2 or Table A1? UNAMBIGUOUSLY S1, S2, S3. "Each appendix must number items as S1, S2, S3... (separate numbering for figures and tables in one file) in order of appearance." "Table A1" is not a JMIR form.
- May one appendix contain multiple sections? Multiple ITEMS: yes, explicitly ("we allow multiple items in a single Multimedia Appendix file"). Multiple SECTIONS: not addressed either way, and therefore permitted by silence.

SHORT ANSWER: I could not find a single published JMIR paper whose Multimedia Appendix is divided into "Part A / Part B / Part C". I opened four JMIR appendices end-to-end — including two that are longer than the manuscript's own (Tables S1–S19 in one; 1009 paragraphs of tables + figures + code in another) — and all four are flat. The author's instinct is right: they have never seen a Part-structured JMIR appendix because it appears not to be a thing JMIR does.

WHAT I ACTUALLY DID. Four appendix files were downloaded and their text extracted programmatically (DOCX unzipped and word/document.xml parsed; the legacy .doc read via its UTF-16 streams), so the structures below are read off the real files, not off search snippets or landing pages. Two additional JMIR appendix PDFs I pulled turned out to be image-only scans with no extractable text and are not counted. Targeted searches for the phrases "Part A of Multimedia Appendix" / "Part B of Multimedia Appendix" / "Part A in Multimedia Appendix" returned zero JMIR articles — only JMIR's own help pages and unrelated appendix-correction notices.

THE PATTERN, ACROSS ALL FOUR. JMIR appendices organize by ITEM NUMBER, and where a grouping heading exists at all it is by CONTENT TYPE, never by Part:
- Zero organizing headings, just Table S1..Sn then Figure S1..Sn (dyslipidemia e81130; the top-level heading is literally the two words "Supplementary Material").
- One word "Appendix", then Figures S1–S6 then Tables S1–S9 (heart failure e54363).
- An auto-generated table of contents with page numbers, then Figures S1–S6 and Tables S1–S19 (CABG e68509). This is the important one: it is the closest in scale to the 29-page manuscript, and it solves the navigation problem the Parts were invented to solve by using a hyperlinked TOC instead.
- Three content-type headings — "Supplementary Tables", "Supplementary Figures", "Supplementary Code" — with tables flat S1–S6 and only the code sub-labelled C1/C2/C3 (JMIR AI e44909). This is the nearest thing to Parts I found anywhere in JMIR, and it is still not Parts.

THE MOST DIRECTLY DAMNING COMPARISON. JMIR Med Inform 2026;14:e81130 is almost the same paper structurally: an Algorithm Development and Validation Study, one discovery cohort, external validation in two more countries, TRIPOD+AI checklist, variable harmonization across cohorts, hyperparameters, missingness, sensitivity analyses, calibration. Its appendix puts the harmonization crosswalk — precisely the content this manuscript elevates to "Part A" — in as plain "Table S2. Variable harmonization scheme and mapping rules for aligning external cohorts to the discovery cohort." No Part. Its published caption is "Supplementary tables (S1-S9) and figures (S1-S4) supporting the main findings of this study."

TWO CONCRETE PROBLEMS WITH THE CURRENT STRUCTURE, independent of taste:
1. The Parts as listed are internally broken. "Part A ... (with numbered subsections A.1 to A.5, B.1 to B.6)" puts B-numbered subsections inside Part A, and then Part B is a separate Part. Whatever the intent, a reader or copyeditor will read that as an error.
2. "Multimedia Appendix 1, Part D" is uncitable under JMIR's rules. JMIR defines exactly one addressing scheme inside an appendix — the S-number — and exactly one citation template, item-first: "Table S7 in Multimedia Appendix 1". There is no sanctioned way to write "Part D". The e44909 authors hit this same wall and worked around it by naming the heading in prose: "...refer to R Code for Data Processing", not "Part C".

WHAT I WOULD DO WITH THIS EVIDENCE. Flatten. Concretely, the layout that matches every JMIR precedent I verified: a hyperlinked table of contents on page 1 (as e68509 does), then "Supplementary Methods" as one content-type heading, then "Supplementary Results" with Tables S1–S16 in strict order of first citation in the main text, then supplementary figures, then the appendix's own stand-alone reference list. Fix the main-text citations to "Table S7 in Multimedia Appendix 1". For the current "Part D" citations, either name the section in prose or — better and fully supported by JMIR's "one file per appendix" rule — split the supplementary methods out as Multimedia Appendix 2, which is the journal's own default for separable content and gives you a citable label.

ONE HONEST CAVEAT ON THE NEGATIVE. Appendix files are separate binaries and are not indexed by search engines, so no search can prove "no JMIR paper anywhere uses Parts". What I can say is: four long JMIR appendices opened, four flat; JMIR's rules define no Part; and phrase searches for Part-style citations in JMIR main texts returned nothing. That is as strong as a negative gets here, and it points the same direction as the author's own reading experience.

MINOR BUT USEFUL, spotted while reading e54363: its flat appendix contains two different tables both labelled "Table S2" and no "Table S3". JMIR states plainly that appendices "are not copyedited by the publishing team", so numbering errors do ship. With 16 tables spread over four Parts, renumbering risk is real — another argument for one flat, sequential run.

ASSIGNMENT SCOPE: I was asked to look OUTSIDE JMIR, at comparable medical / health-informatics journals that publish prediction-model studies, and determine whether "Part A / Part B" divisions inside a single supplementary file actually occur, and what the dominant convention is. I opened and read 13 real supplementary files (not snippets) across Lancet Digital Health, JAMA Network Open, JAMA Psychiatry, BMJ, npj Digital Medicine, Kidney International Reports and NEJM.

I found exactly ONE unambiguous case of a single supplementary file divided into literal "Part A / Part B": the Anti-PLA2R1 antibodies paper, Kidney International Reports 2021 (doi:10.1016/j.ekir.2021.04.002). Its mmc1.pdf (14 pp) opens "Supplementary Tables  Supplementary Appendix part A: N=168 full cohort" and later "Supplementary Appendix part B: N=156 incident patients". Critically, the S-numbering RESTARTS inside each Part - Table S1 exists in Part A and again in Part B - which forces every main-text citation to carry the Part label: "Supplementary Appendix Part B Table S1", "Supplementary Appendix Part A Tables 1-4", "Supplementary Appendix Part B Table S4b" (verbatim from the article's full text). This is the concrete failure mode of Part-structuring.
I found ONE near-miss that is the best supportive precedent for the author: the GSU-Pulmonary Score paper, Lancet Digital Health 2024 (doi:10.1016/S2589-7500(24)00065-7). Its single long eAppendix keeps ONE flat numbered series of figures/tables (Supplementary figure 1-8, Supplementary table 1-5) and then appends the long prose blocks as lettered appendices: "Appendix A. Full definitions of predictor variables and clinical outcomes .... 16", "Appendix B. Independent PROBAST assessment (16) .... 22", "Appendix C. Collaborating authors (PubMed-citable) .... 33". Note the asymmetry: lettering is used ONLY for the trailing prose annexes; the tables are never put inside a lettered part. The main text still cites by page: "Full definitions are included in the appendix (pp 16-21)", "(appendix pp 22-30)".
I also chased two apparent "Part A" hits that turned out to be FALSE POSITIVES, reported so nobody re-finds them and misreads them: JAMA Psychiatry 2026 TSND-201 (doi:10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2025.4625) has "eAppendix. Part A of IMPACT-1 (Open-Label)" where "Part A" is a phase of the trial, not a division of the appendix; and JAMA Netw Open 2022 e2227109, where the hit was a figure panel. Neither is evidence for Part-structured appendices.

ANSWER 2 - WHAT IS THE DOMINANT CONVENTION? Overwhelmingly: ONE flat, typed, sequentially numbered series inside one file, with a front table of contents once the file gets long, and NO Part/Section wrapper. Three sub-dialects, all flat:
(a) Lancet family - flat TOC with PAGE NUMBERS; the main text cites pages, never sections. PIERS-ML (Lancet Digit Health 2024;6:e238-50) is the closest analogue to this manuscript: 29 pages, the exact size in question, laid out as "Table S1 ... pp 2-4" through "Table S7 ... p 15", then "PIERS-ML Data Sharing Statement p 16", then "PIERS-ML Statistical Supplement pp 17-25" LAST. Tables first in one unbroken run, methods prose parked at the end as one named block - no Parts.
(b) JAMA family - eMethods / eTable / eFigure / eAppendix / eReferences, each type independently numbered, INTERLEAVED in the order the main text needs them, no grouping headers (Ravaut et al., JAMA Netw Open 2021: "eFigure 1 / eMethods 1 / eTable 1 / eTable 2 / eMethods 2 / eMethods 3 / eFigure 2-4 / eTable 3-4 / eReferences"). When there is more than one prose block, JAMA NUMBERS them ("eAppendix 1. Survey Instrument", "eAppendix 2. Response Rate Calculation") rather than lettering Parts.
(c) Springer Nature / npj Digital Medicine - a front contents list of typed series: Supplementary Figure 1-8, Supplementary Table 1-10, Supplementary Data 1-7, Supplementary Note 1-6 (npj Digit Med sepsis-trajectory paper, doi:10.1038/s41746-026-02565-x). Methods prose lives in "Supplementary Note N", which is the Nature-portfolio equivalent of the author's Part A and Part D - a numbered item in the same flat series, not a container wrapped around tables.
BMJ letters ITEMS rather than numbering them, but is still flat: QCOVID (BMJ 2020;371:m3731) is a 28-page single file running Supplementary Box A, Supplementary Table A-G, Supplementary Figure A-H, cited as "supplementary tables A and B", "Supplementary table G". The letter replaces the number; it does not create a Part.
The only long appendix I read that uses containers is the NEJM PREDIMED 2018 appendix (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1800389): a page-numbered TOC of "1. PREDIMED Investigators ... 4", "3. Randomization procedures and deviations from protocol ... 8", with "Fig. S1" and "Fig. S2" interleaved - and even there the S-numbering is one continuous series across sections. That is the closest sanctioned analogue to Part-structuring: NUMBERED sections, CONTINUOUS S-numbering, PAGE NUMBERS in the TOC.

PRACTICAL READ-ACROSS. Nothing in the comparator literature forbids internal divisions, and GSU-Pulmonary and PREDIMED show a long appendix can carry named or numbered blocks. But three features of the current structure have no support in anything I opened:
1. Splitting the TABLES across Parts (S1-S10 in Part B, S11-S16 in Part C). No comparator does this - every flat-series journal, and even the GSU lettered appendix, keeps ONE unbroken table run. This is precisely what broke in the Kidney Int Rep example.
2. Subsection numbering that runs A.1-A.5 then B.1-B.6 inside a block already called "Part A". No comparator has anything like it; the letter prefixes collide with the Part letters. (Putting methods LAST is fine - PIERS-ML does exactly that - it is the Part wrapper and the A.*/B.* numbering that are unsupported.)
3. The citation form "Multimedia Appendix 1, Part D". Nothing in the comparator set cites a supplement by named part except the Kidney Int Rep paper, which only had to because its numbering restarted. Everyone else cites a page (Lancet), a typed item ("eTable 3 in the Supplement", JAMA; "Supplementary table G", BMJ), or a numbered note (Nature).
RECOMMENDATION ON THIS EVIDENCE: flatten. Keep one continuous Table S1..S16 run; convert Parts A-D into either (i) plain headings inside a Supplementary Methods / Supplementary Results split, or (ii) numbered sections with a page-numbered TOC in the PREDIMED/Lancet style. If any lettering is retained, follow GSU-Pulmonary and letter ONLY the trailing prose annexes (harmonization crosswalk, predictor-set amendment), never the table run.

NOTE: JMIR's own requirements were another agent's assignment; I checked them only to confirm my cross-journal advice does not contradict them. Source: JMIR Publications support knowledge base, "What are the guidelines for supplementary files (figures, multimedia appendices, additional material for reviewers/editors only)?" - https://support.jmir.org/hc/en-us/articles/115002199367-What-are-the-guidelines-for-supplementary-files-figures-multimedia-appendices-additional-material-for-reviewers-editors-only (fetched 2026-08-04; the page returns 403 to a plain fetcher, retrieved with a normal browser user-agent).

The governing passage, verbatim:
"Of note, we allow multiple items in a single Multimedia Appendix file. However, please ensure that each individual item (eg, figure or table) is named as "Table S1, Table S2, Figure S1, Figure S2) within the Multimedia Appendix. Each appendix must number items as S1, S2, S3... (separate numbering for figures and tables in one file) in order of appearance."

On citation, verbatim:
"If you wish to specifically cite these supplementary tables or figures in the text to draw the reader's attention to them, please refer to them as follows:
"...as shown in Figure S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1"
"...performed better than the control group (Table S2 in Multimedia Appendix 3)""

Other verbatim rules from the same page that bear on a 29-page appendix:
- "Multimedia Appendices (MAs) are published at the end of a paper."
- "Note: MAs are not copyedited by the publishing team, and it is therefore the authors' responsibility to ensure relevance, accuracy, and completeness of each MA file."
- "Do not include a title (first) page as the manuscript title is likely to change during the production process."
- "One file per appendix. Multiple files should not be zipped (compressed, packed) together, they should be uploaded as separate supplementary files and referred to as separate Multimedia Appendices in the manuscript"
- "Please do not include the MA label/number in the caption, like Multimedia Appendix 1 or Supplementary file 2, etc. These labels will be added automatically by our script during typesetting."
- "In addition, MAs should be mentioned in sequential order in the main manuscript."
- "References cited within a multimedia appendix (MA) should have a corresponding, stand-alone reference list within that same MA file, even if some references overlap with the main manuscript's reference list."
- Accepted formats: ".png, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt, .pptx, .pdf, .txt, .mov, .mp4, .avi, .zip, .rar, .7z."

The general Instructions for Authors page (https://www.jmir.org/author-information/instructions-for-authors) says only: "[optional] Multimedia Appendix of supplementary files (e.g. a PowerPoint presentation of a conference talk about the study, additional screenshots of a website, mpeg/ Quicktime video or audio files, or Excel, Access, SAS, or SPSS files containing original data)" - it is silent on internal structure.

Bearing on the Part question: JMIR names exactly one internal organising device for a multi-item appendix - the S1/S2/S3 series, numbered "in order of appearance", separately for tables and figures. It says nothing about Parts, so Parts are not forbidden; but the sanctioned in-text citation form is "Table S7 in Multimedia Appendix 1", not "Multimedia Appendix 1, Table S7", and there is no addressable citation form for a "Part". That matches what I found across the comparator journals: they cite pages or typed items, never parts.

## 1. JMIR에 Part 구조 부록이 실제로 존재하는가 — 사실상 없음

**증거로 말하면: 확인된 사례 0건.** 세 차례 검색에서 JMIR 계열 부록 파일 6개를 실제로 내려받아 본문 텍스트까지 추출해 열어봤고, 전부 flat이었습니다.

| 논문 | 부록 실제 구조 | Part? |
|---|---|---|
| Woo S, Yon DK, et al. *Machine Learning Prediction Model for Dyslipidemia... Algorithm Development and Validation Study.* JMIR Med Inform 2026;14:e81130. doi:10.2196/81130 | 최상위 제목이 "Supplementary Material" 한 줄, 이후 Table S1–S9 → Figure S1–S4 일렬. **조화 크로스워크가 그냥 "Table S2. Variable harmonization scheme and mapping rules for aligning external cohorts to the discovery cohort."** | 없음 |
| *Machine Learning Models... Gastrointestinal Bleeding After CABG.* J Med Internet Res 2025;27:e68509. doi:10.2196/68509 | 6.6 MB, Table S1–S19 + Figure S1–S6. 유일한 구조 장치는 **페이지번호 달린 자동생성 목차** | 없음 |
| *Machine Learning for the Prediction of Procedural Case Durations: Algorithm Development and Validation Study.* JMIR AI 2023;2:e44909. doi:10.2196/44909 | 1009 문단, 표+그림+코드 혼재. 구분 표제가 **내용 유형별**: "Supplementary Tables" / "Supplementary Figures" / "Supplementary Code". 표는 S1–S6 일렬 | 없음 |
| Adams J, et al. *Real-World Meditation App Engagement.* JMIR Mhealth Uhealth 2026;14:e79366. doi:10.2196/79366 | 12개 내부 섹션 + 점선 목차. 섹션 이름이 **"Supplementary 1." … "Supplementary 12."**, 표는 섹션을 가로질러 S1–S13 연속 | 없음 |
| Gao Z, et al. *Improving the Prognostic Evaluation Precision... Multimodal Deep Learning Model.* J Med Internet Res 2024;26:e54363. doi:10.2196/54363 | "Appendix" 한 단어 후 Figure S1–S6, Table S1–S9 (S2가 두 번, S3 없음 — 오류 그대로 출판) | 없음 |
| *Harnessing Moderate-Sized Language Models... Algorithm Development, Validation, and Implementation Study.* JMIR AI 2025;4:e57828. doi:10.2196/57828 | 반대 전략: 부록을 **4개 파일로 분리**, 내부 구분 없음 | 없음 |

메인 텍스트 구문 검색("Part A of Multimedia Appendix", "Part A in Multimedia Appendix")도 JMIR 전 계열에서 0건.

**정직한 한계:** 부록은 별도 바이너리라 검색엔진이 색인하지 않으므로 "JMIR 전체에 없다"는 증명은 불가능합니다. 다만 (i) 실제로 연 6건 전부 flat, (ii) JMIR 규정에 Part라는 개념 자체가 없음, (iii) 인용 구문 검색 0건 — 부정적 증거로는 이 정도가 한계치이고, 저자의 독서 경험과 방향이 일치합니다.

**JMIR 밖에서는?** 딱 한 건 명확한 Part 사례가 있고, 그게 오히려 반면교사입니다: Seifert L, et al. *Anti-PLA2R1 Antibodies as Prognostic Biomarker in Membranous Nephropathy.* Kidney Int Rep 2021;6(10):2618-2628. doi:10.1016/j.ekir.2021.04.002 — mmc1.pdf가 "Supplementary Appendix part A: N=168 full cohort" / "part B: N=156 incident patients"로 갈리고 **S 번호가 Part마다 재시작**해서, 본문이 매번 "Supplementary Appendix Part B Table S1", "Supplementary Appendix Part A Tables 1-4"라고 써야 하는 상태가 됐습니다.

가장 크기가 비슷한 대조군(29페이지, 동일)은 flat입니다: Montgomery-Csoban T, et al. *Machine learning-enabled maternal risk assessment (PIERS-ML).* Lancet Digit Health 2024;6(4):e238-e250. doi:10.1016/S2589-7500(23)00267-4 — Table S1–S7 한 줄기 → "PIERS-ML Statistical Supplement pp 17-25"를 **맨 뒤에** 배치. 방법론을 뒤에 두는 건 괜찮다는 뜻입니다. 문제는 Part 껍데기입니다.

## 2. JMIR 규정 — 강제 vs 관행

출처: support.jmir.org, "What are the guidelines for supplementary files..." (https://support.jmir.org/hc/en-us/articles/115002199367). Instructions for Authors 본페이지는 부록 내부에 대해 사실상 침묵.

**강제(규정 문구):**
- "Each appendix must number items as S1, S2, S3... (separate numbering for figures and tables in one file) **in order of appearance**."
- 인용 문법 — 항목이 먼저, 부록 번호가 뒤: "...as shown in **Figure S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1**" / "(**Table S2 in Multimedia Appendix 3**)"
- "One file per appendix."
- "References cited within a multimedia appendix (MA) should have a corresponding, stand-alone reference list within that same MA file."
- "Do not include a title (first) page"; 캡션에 "Multimedia Appendix 1"을 넣지 말 것 (자동 부여, 중복 라벨 발생).
- "MAs should be mentioned in sequential order in the main manuscript."

**관행(규정 아님):** Part든 섹션이든 내부 구획은 **금지되어 있지 않습니다.** "MAs are not copyedited by the publishing team", "published largely as submitted" — 내부는 저자 책임. 다만 JMIR가 정의한 유일한 주소 체계는 S 번호이므로, **"Part D"는 인용할 수 있는 주소가 아닙니다.**

## 3. 권고: (b) 평탄화 — 단, 목차를 붙인 형태

구체적으로:

1. 1페이지에 **하이퍼링크 목차**(e68509 방식). 29페이지의 탐색 문제는 Part가 아니라 TOC로 푸는 것이 JMIR의 실제 선례입니다.
2. `Supplementary Methods` — 현 Part D + Part A의 조화/변수 개정 서술. 하위는 A.1/B.1이 아니라 평범한 소제목 또는 "Supplementary 1., 2., ..."(e79366 선례).
3. `Supplementary Results` — **Table S1..Sn을 본문 최초 인용 순서대로 끊김 없이** 한 줄기. 현재 Part B(S1–S10)/Part C(S11–S16) 분할은 폐기.
4. 본문 인용을 규정 문법으로 교체: `Multimedia Appendix 1, Table S7` → **`Table S7 in Multimedia Appendix 1`**. `Multimedia Appendix 1, Part D` → **`Supplementary Methods in Multimedia Appendix 1`**.
5. 부록 자체 참고문헌 목록 포함, 제목 페이지 제거, 캡션에서 "Multimedia Appendix 1" 삭제.
6. **표 개수 감사 필수**: 22개 표인데 S16까지만 있습니다. 22개면 S1–S22여야 하고, 나머지가 그림이면 Figure S1.. 별도 계열로. 지금 상태로는 규정 위반입니다.
7. Word 자동 PDF 변환 시 넓은 표가 오른쪽 여백에서 잘립니다 — **직접 PDF로 변환해 업로드**.

이유: Part 구조를 지지하는 JMIR 선례가 0건인 반면, 평탄화를 지지하는 선례는 저자 본인 논문과 유형·규모가 거의 같은 것(e81130, e68509, e44909)으로 확보돼 있고, 규정이 정의한 유일한 주소 체계와도 일치합니다.

**부수 지적:** 현재 "Part A ... (with numbered subsections A.1 to A.5, B.1 to B.6)"는 그 자체로 깨져 있습니다 — Part A 안에 B.* 하위절이 있고 별도로 Part B가 또 있습니다. 심사자는 이걸 오류로 읽습니다.

## 4. 선택하지 않은 쪽(Part A–D 유지)의 구체적 위험

- **인용이 무효**: "Part D"는 JMIR가 정의하지 않은 로케이터입니다. 본문은 copyedit되므로 편집자가 이 문자열을 손대고, 대응 대상이 없으니 심사·교정 단계에서 질의(query)로 돌아옵니다.
- **S 번호 순서 규정 위반 유발**: 표 없는 Part A가 맨 앞, 방법론 Part D가 맨 뒤에 오면 "in order of appearance"를 지키기 어렵고, 표를 Part B/C로 쪼갠 상태에서 재배열이 생기면 번호가 어긋납니다. 부록은 copyedit되지 않으므로 **오류가 그대로 출판됩니다** — e54363에는 Table S2가 두 개, S3이 없는 채로 실제 출판돼 있습니다.
- **Kidney Int Rep 실패 경로**: Part 분할이 번호 중복을 낳고, 그 결과 모든 본문 인용이 "Part B Table S1"처럼 길어지는데, JMIR에는 그렇게 쓸 문법이 아예 없습니다.
- **선례 부재 자체의 비용**: 심사자가 처음 보는 형식은 그 자체로 질의를 부릅니다. 얻는 것(가독성)은 TOC로 동일하게 얻을 수 있습니다.
